title: Resident species accounted for 77% of the count-weighted thermal shift at 21 Finnish moth sites
abstract: We split the change in moth community temperature indices into resident composition, recorded entry and recorded loss. We used species counts and European thermal scores from a public Finnish release. At 21 sites with at least five surveys in both 1993-2002 and 2013-2022, the mean count-weighted index rose by 0.248 C. An exact symmetric split assigned 0.191 C, or 77% (95% spatial-block interval 66-84%), to species recorded in both windows. Entry added 0.052 C and loss added 0.005 C. Equal survey counts gave a 71% resident share; removal of the largest positive resident contributor gave 76%. Annual presence weights gave 47%, which shows that the inferred pathway depends on the weighting. Sixteen sites were in southern Finland. The release overlaps earlier Finnish work and is not an independent replication of it. Recorded status is not a demographic state. Detection, effort, shared year shocks and source filtering limit inference. The result adds a measured constraint on models of thermal change but does not establish climate causation or explain the gap in birds. Code, aggregate results, source hashes, a figure and external-data retrieval instructions are included.
